title: Write back only the customers a request changed

blocks.text: This practice builds on the previous one: `CustomerSession` now gives each request one object per customer. Requests change those objects, and the changes have to reach the database without every caller remembering to save. The first attempt wrote every customer the request had read, and the database team counts four `UPDATE`s for a request that changed one tier.

items: `remember(customer)`: keep what the session will compare against; `find` calls it after each load;
`isDirty(customer)`: whether the customer now differs from that;
`flush()`: write every changed customer with `writeRow`, and return how many it wrote.

blocks.text: A request changes customers through their fields and through their tag lists, may set a field to the value it already has, and may flush more than once. About ten lines in total.
The tests run against H2 in memory through a connection that counts the `UPDATE` statements it executes.

cases.says: a customer renamed during the session has the new name in its row after flush, and the others keep theirs
a flush after reads only leaves every row as it was
a tag added to a customer's tag list is a change, and flush writes it
flush sends one UPDATE per changed customer and none for customers that were only read
a field set to a new object with the same value is not a change and is not written
after a flush, the written values are the new baseline: a second flush writes nothing until something changes again

origin.section: Flush Writes What Differs From the Snapshot Taken at Load

concepts: At flush each managed entity is compared by value with the snapshot taken at load; only entities that differ get an UPDATE, and a field set to an equal value is not a change.
